# HealthKit

<!-- generated:header (isim/tools/coverage-summary.py; do not edit by hand) -->
**Symbols:** 15.8% of Apple's iOS API (422 of 2672, exact) · **Rows:** 5: 1 🟡 4 ❌ · **iOS:** 8.0+
<!-- /generated:header -->

**Area:** [Location, personal data & sensors](../COVERAGE.md#location) · **Apple:** [HealthKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/healthkit) · **Issues:** [`area:location`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Alocation)

## How isim implements it

- **Adapted:** a JSON sample store (`isim/swift/overlays/HealthKit/Store.swift`) and the Health access sheet.
- **Objective-C / C interface:** headers in `isim/sdk-src/Frameworks/HealthKit` over the overlay's classes; not yet
  `HKStatisticsCollectionQuery` and `dateOfBirthComponents` (isim's Foundation has no `NSDateComponents`).

## API

| API / feature | Status | iOS | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| HealthKit | 🟡 | ≤17 | `isHealthDataAvailable` true on iPhone; Health Access sheet (per-type write/read switches, Turn On All) remembered per app; quantity/category samples stored in `$ISIM_DATA/Library/Health`, unit conversion, sample/statistics/statistics-collection/observer queries; read denial hidden like iOS; no workouts, characteristics unset, no clinical records. Missing: workouts, correlations, activity summaries; characteristics are fixed. Tested: test_personal |
| Workout types: `HKWorkoutActivityType` (Apple's raw values), `HKWorkoutSessionLocationType`, `HKWorkoutSwimmingLocationType` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: the enums WorkoutKit's plans use; workouts, workout sessions and builders are not in isim yet. Tested (HelloAccessories: test_devices, through WorkoutKit) |
| Objective-C interface: `HKHealthStore` (availability, authorization, save, delete, execute, stop, biological sex), `HKObjectType` and its subclasses with the type identifier constants, `HKUnit`, `HKQuantity`, `HKSource`, `HKSourceRevision`, `HKDevice`, `HKObject`, `HKSample`, `HKQuantitySample`, `HKCategorySample`, `HKQuery` predicates, `HKSampleQuery`, `HKStatisticsQuery`, `HKStatistics`, `HKObserverQuery`, `HKErrorDomain` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: the overlay's classes under Apple's Objective-C names and selectors, the same store and sheet as Swift. Tested (HelloSensorsObjC: test_sensors_objc) |
| Anchored object queries: `HKAnchoredObjectQuery` (`init(type:predicate:anchor:limit:resultsHandler:)`, `updateHandler`), `HKQueryAnchor` (`init(fromValue:)`, NSSecureCoding), `HKDeletedObject` (`uuid`, `metadata`) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: the device's Health database numbers its changes (samples saved before 0.26 count as 0); an anchor is the last number a query saw, and a deletion leaves a tombstone. The first query (no anchor) returns no deletions, as on iOS; the limit counts samples and deletions; `updateHandler` runs after each save or delete while the query runs. Tested (HelloSensors: test_sensors_and_health, every iOS version; HelloSensorsObjC: test_sensors_objc) |
| `HKSourceQuery` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: the apps that saved the samples this app may see (all apps when it may read the type, else only itself). Tested (HelloSensors, HelloSensorsObjC) |
| Swift query descriptors (iOS 15.4): `HKSampleQueryDescriptor` (`result(for:)` with `SortDescriptor` and a limit), `HKAnchoredObjectQueryDescriptor` (`result(for:)`, `results(for:)` with `Result`: `addedSamples`, `deletedObjects`, `newAnchor`), `HKSourceQueryDescriptor`, `HKSamplePredicate` (`.sample`, `.quantitySample`, `.categorySample`), `HKAsyncQuery`, `HKAsyncSequenceQuery` | ✅ | ≤17 | on the queries above: one query per predicate; `results(for:)` yields the first result and then each change, and stops its queries when the iteration ends. Tested (HelloSensors) |
| Background delivery: `HKHealthStore.enableBackgroundDelivery(for:frequency:withCompletion:)`, `disableBackgroundDelivery(for:withCompletion:)`, `disableAllBackgroundDelivery(completion:)`, the async variants, `HKUpdateFrequency` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: the registrations are kept per app (`$ISIM_DATA/Library/Health/background.json`) and logged; while the app runs its observer and anchored queries see changes at once. isim does not launch a suspended app in the background, and does not check the background-delivery entitlement. Tested (HelloSensors, HelloSensorsObjC) |
